I rewrote the three writable modules; no other files were touched.

**`src/merge.mjs`** — replaced the mutating `Object.assign(defaults, file, env)` (which mutated the exported `DEFAULTS` and dropped nested siblings) with a non-mutating merge that builds fresh `network`/`ui` objects field-by-field across defaults → file → env, so a partial nested override keeps its siblings and no layer reference is retained. `undefined` values are skipped, so `0`/`false` survive.

**`src/env-config.mjs`** — replaced truthiness checks with `!== undefined` presence checks, so `APP_RETRIES=0`/`APP_ENABLED=false` are honored. Added strict parsing: retries must match `/^[0-9]+/` (leading zeros allowed) and be a safe integer ≤ `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`; compact/enabled must be exactly `"true"`/`"false"`; endpoint/theme must be nonempty strings. Invalid recognized values throw `TypeError`; unrecognized keys are ignored.

**`src/validate.mjs`** — tightened retries to `Number.isSafeInteger` with the upper bound, and now returns a fresh deep-copied object so results never alias inputs or defaults.

`src/index.mjs`, `src/defaults.mjs`, `src/file-config.mjs`, `src/format.mjs`, `src/legacy.mjs`, and the utilities were left unchanged, preserving the exported API and legacy/format output.

**Checked:** I read all source files and the public test file and verified the logic by inspection against each documented case (defaults, nested file merge, env precedence with `"00"`/`"false"`, no cross-call state). No tests were executed — there is no shell/test runner available in this environment.
